issue_context.title: System.IO.Compression.ZipFile.CreateFromDirectory: overloads to write to  a stream rather than a file

review_comments: FWIW, you don't actually need to dispose of MemoryStream.

I see that calling the empty dispose on MemoryStream is not vaporized in codegen. Should it be/can it be? It's arguably cleaner to dispose everything disposable, eg., presumably that is helpful for some static analyzer.
cc @AndyAyersMS 

I don't think we're consistent for MemoryStream

In general, the JIT should inline empty methods, if they're called directly. However it may not inline the version that is left in a residual fault clause if the `using` entails a `try {...}  finally {...}`  (some do, some don't) and the JIT decides to clone the finally.

If you can point us at a repro case either @egorbo or I will investigate.

I was looking at https://sharplab.io/#v2:EYLgxg9gTgpgtADwGwBYA0AXEBDAzgWwB8BYAKAAEAmARjPIAYACc6gOgEkB5AbjLoGZmlRgA0yAbzKNpzakmYpGAMWoAKAJRSZk0jL3MmAN2xRG+XIwC8jAHYwA7owCyMfNACeAZQyxs+Dby6+tIAwhA2uBAANjCsAOpQAJYYMKrmrAAyMDYA5hgAFuqBegC+WtLlsvLkikqUGpU6wdLGpuZWtg7Orh7evv5FlXphEdGxCcmp6Vm5BYNB0mWkS3qVQA

(not sure how to tell what version sharplab is using)
So perhaps we should dispose all MemoryStreams to avoid pressure on the finalization queue.

a) There's no pressure on the finalization queue: MemoryStream doesn't define a finalizer.
b) Calling SuppressFinalize on a finalizable object doesn't remove it from the queue; it simply sets a bit in its header to say "dear finalizer thread, when you get around to processing this object, skip it".
Trying to make sure I understand: MemoryStream Dispose calls SuppressFinalize() as a perf optimization, but it's small enough that it's OK to not dispose?

SuppressFinalize is a nop / pure overhead if an object doesn't have a finalizer.  MemoryStream.Dispose calls SuppressFinalize in case a type derived from MemoryStream adds a finalizer and this instance is actually an instance of that derived type; it's following the Dispose pattern.  If you just construct a MemoryStream and not something derived from it, Dispose it, and never try to use it again, that Dispose call is pure overhead with zero benefit.  For sure it's a small overhead, but that's why you see us (and a ton of code) not bothering, because it doesn't matter for MemoryStream.

Would it be possible to add a check for the concrete type within the Dispose, so that if the type was not derived it would elide the content of Dispose, improving the code for anyone unnecessarily calling it?

What are you trying to avoid, the virtual call to Dispose(bool)?  That's necessary in the general case as it contains all of the `x = false` lines that result in exceptions being thrown from subsequent usage, that transition CanXx properties from returning true to false, etc.

I'm not seeing the value of trying to microoptimize these calls.  It's simply the case that code doesn't need to contort itself to dispose of a MemoryStream it itself created.  It can if it likes, but it needn't.
